summary: Canadian Coast Guard light on the Lucy Islands, Chatham Sound, near Prince Rupert: lit 1 January 1907, concrete tower 1960, last keeper 1988; closed, boat access only.

structures.note: White octagonal tower with red top (Canadian Coast Guard); 10.5 m (35 ft) per the Lighthouse Directory.
The 1907 light was a rectangular wooden dwelling with a white square wooden lantern (Department report printed 1908). The sources read do not say what became of it.

access.note: Site and tower closed; accessible only by boat (Lighthouse Directory).

facts.ownership: Federal, Canadian Coast Guard (Lighthouse Directory; LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Put in operation on 1 January 1907 (Department report printed 1908); station established 1907 (Lighthouse Directory).
Rectangular wooden dwelling with white square wooden lantern.
Air diaphone in a frame building beside the light placed in operation (LighthouseFriends).
Present octagonal concrete tower erected with a new single dwelling, by Stange Construction (LighthouseFriends; Lighthouse Directory gives 1960).
Last keeper, Ike Pronk, transferred in July 1988; the station was left unstaffed (LighthouseFriends).
Keeper's dwelling burned by a contractor the next month (LighthouseFriends). The Lighthouse Directory says the house was demolished in 1988.

keepers.name: L. Lindblow
keepers.note: Also spelled Linbloom or Lindbloom (LighthouseFriends). Hired as first keeper; taken to hospital at Port Simpson after a paralytic shock. The 1908 list gives no appointment date (read from the page image).

keepers.name: Joseph Stanislaus Octave Ouellette
keepers.note: Listed as J. O. Ouellette at Lucy Island in the 1912 list, appointed 6 July 1910 (date read from the page image, printed p. 250). Family moved to the island in 1910; a fourth child was born there in 1913; his wife died in 1919.

keepers.name: Frank Glinn
keepers.note: Public role only, as LighthouseFriends lists it; the present concrete tower was built during his time.

keepers.name: Frederick Pratt
keepers.note: Same name appears in the Ballenas Islands roster for 1970 to 1989; not linked, as the name alone does not connect them.

keepers.name: J. Keith Nuttall
keepers.note: The same name appears in the Ballenas Islands roster for 1989 to 1993; not linked, as the name alone does not connect them.

keepers.name: Ike Pronk
keepers.note: Last keeper; transferred to McInnes Lighthouse in July 1988.

corrections.why: The concrete tower in the record was built in 1960 (LighthouseFriends; Lighthouse Directory). The 1907 light was a wooden dwelling with a square wooden lantern (Department report printed 1908).
The Coast Guard dropped its plan in 1987, but the last keeper left in July 1988 and the dwelling was gone or demolished that year (LighthouseFriends; Lighthouse Directory).
Same as the automated event: the last keeper left in 1988.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikidata's 1960 is the year of the present concrete tower; the Lighthouse Directory's 1907 is the station's establishment and first lighting with the wooden dwelling. Both are right for different structures.

Wikidata gives automation in 1987. LighthouseFriends says the last keeper was transferred in July 1988 after the 1987 plan was dropped, and the Lighthouse Directory says the dwelling was demolished in 1988. The 1988 date is used.
The Lighthouse Directory gives a focal plane of 21.5 m; the Coast Guard list gives 21.6 m. The Coast Guard figure is used.
The Lighthouse Directory puts the light about 15 km (10 mi) west of Prince Rupert; LighthouseFriends says roughly 17 km (11 mi). The story gives the Directory figure and states LighthouseFriends's.

notes_for_editor: (1) LighthouseFriends is the only source for the Lindblow hospital passage, the Ouellette family details (memoir-based), the 1924 lens, the 1927 diaphone, Stange Construction and the rhinoceros auklet colony; none was checked against a primary source, and the story attributes each to LighthouseFriends. (2) Verified on the page images this pass. 1908 list (printed p. 149, scan 156): Lindblow, L, Lucy Island, salary 600, with no appointment date; the 'Aug. July' OCR belongs to the rows above. 1912 list (printed p. 250, scan 257): R. Pollock at Lennard Island, J. O. Ouellette at Lucy Island appointed 6 July 1910, W. T. Franklin at Merry Island; matched by row on the image, the date is not in the OCR quote. (3) Distance: LighthouseFriends gives roughly 17 km (11 mi) west of Prince Rupert; the Lighthouse Directory gives 15 km (10 mi). The story states both. Focal height: Coast Guard 21.6 m; Directory 21.5 m; the story uses the Coast Guard figure and states the Directory's. (4) The 1960 date for the present tower rests on LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory; the corpus Department series is not searched for it. (5) Keepers after about 1960 (Glinn to 1963, Pronk 1988, and the others on the roster) are listed from LighthouseFriends in their public role only. The story uses only Glinn's service dates and Pronk's transfer. LighthouseFriends's 1963 account of Glinn's household is not used. (6) Name matches with no recorded link: J. Keith Nuttall (Lucy 1977 to 1981, Ballenas 1989 to 1993) and Frederick Pratt (Lucy 1963 to 1970, Ballenas 1970 to 1989). (7) Two accounts of the keeper's house: burned by a contractor the month after July 1988 (LighthouseFriends) and demolished in 1988 (Directory). The story gives both. (8) Wikipedia used only for leads and not cited. (9) Newspapers not searched: British Columbia papers are not in Chronicling America. (10) The record's Commons photo has no licence in the record; none added. (11) Fiscal periods: the 1907 volume is the fiscal year ended June 30, 1906; the 1908 volume the nine months ended March 31, 1907; the 1912 volume fiscal 1910-11.
